steps.message:
Item 051 on the Package A verification register is assigned to me and falls due on 07/20/2026, two days before the Level-3 placement. It covers the Block C spread footings and the long-term settlement of the clay beneath them.

Work through Item 051 against the project record and issue the verification memo. Set out what you reviewed, the basis you applied, your findings with the working behind them, and the disposition. Where something has to be produced before the item can be closed, say what it is and who is required to produce it.

Use the attached memorandum form and keep its sections. Write it from Rahul Nimkar, Geotechnical Reviewer, to Adrian Vance, Project Engineer, copied to Rachel Marlbeck. Save it as Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item051_BlockC.docx.
I'll start by exploring the project record.

1.  EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. has completed a subsurface investigation and geotechnical engineering analysis for
Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, Ohio.
Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared podium, with
a single basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
Block B.
The finished design grade across Package A is established at El. 750.0 ft. Existing ground surface stands at
approximately El. 750.0 across the footprints of Blocks A and C but falls to about El. 738.0 across the Block B
footprint (a former surface drainage swale). Placement of engineered fill of variable thickness — up to
approximately 12 ft beneath Block B — will therefore be required to bring the site to design grade.
The subsurface profile consists of three principal strata:
•  Stratum 1 — Upper sand, classified SP-SM (poorly-graded sand with silt), medium-dense, from
existing grade down to El. 738.0, total unit weight 118 pcf.
•  Stratum 2 — Compressible clay aquitard, classified CL (lean clay of medium plasticity),
normally-consolidated, from El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0 (18 ft thick), total unit weight 120 pcf, low
permeability. This is the strata governing settlement of shallow foundations and provides the aquitard
between the shallow and deep groundwater regimes.
•  Stratum 3 — Dense sand and gravel aquifer, classified SW-GW, below El. 720.0, total unit weight 130
pcf, confined by the overlying clay.
Groundwater is present as two distinct regimes:
•  The design water table in the upper sand is set at El. 742.0 ft. Piezometer readings taken from three
shallow standpipes over the 11/2024–02/2025 monitoring period range from El. 741.6 to El. 742.4;
groundwater seepage was observed at El. 741.8 to El. 742.2 in the Block A test-pit excavation.
•  A confined piezometric head of El. 738.0 ft has been measured in the deep sand-and-gravel aquifer
through two deep piezometers screened below El. 720.0, with readings ranging El. 737.7 to El. 738.3. The
confined head is at essentially the same elevation as the top of the clay aquitard.
Consolidation testing on two undisturbed Shelby-tube samples of the compressible clay (samples B-06 U3 and
B-08 U2, tested per ASTM D2435) yielded a compression index Cc = 0.28, a recompression index Cr = 0.045,
an initial void ratio e0 = 0.92, an in-situ vertical effective stress σ'0 = 1,850 psf, and a preconsolidation pressure
σ'p = 1,900 psf. The margin (σ'p − σ'0 ≈ 50 psf) confirms the clay is essentially normally-consolidated: any net
stress increase applied at the top of the clay will produce virgin (Cc) compression rather than recompression
(Cr) compression.
Principal geotechnical recommendations are as follows:
1.  Block C — Spread footings may be founded within the upper sand. Consolidation of the underlying
compressible clay under column-load stress increases at mid-depth of the clay must be explicitly computed
by the Structural Engineer of Record, using the parameters provided herein, and reconciled against the
settlement tolerances specified in the project structural criteria.
2.  Blocks A and B basement mat — A conventional reinforced-concrete mat foundation may be founded
within the upper sand at the design underside elevation. Hydrostatic uplift from the El. 742.0 water table
must be resolved by mat self-weight, superimposed permanent loads and, where necessary, tension
elements. The waterproofing system for the below-grade envelope must be selected for the applicable

•  Block B — six-story residential tower over a shared podium, seated on the same basement mat

the block footprint (elevator and mechanical/electrical service space, approximately 24 ft below design
grade).

2.3  Purpose and Scope of Investigation
The purpose of the investigation was to:
•  Characterize the subsurface soil profile, groundwater conditions and hydrogeologic regime across the
Package A footprint;
•  Recover and test representative undisturbed samples of the compressible clay stratum in order to develop
consolidation parameters for foundation-settlement analysis;
•  Provide geotechnical recommendations for the foundation of each block, for the design of the basement
mat and the plant-room excavation, and for the engineered fill required to bring the Block B footprint to
design grade; and
•  Provide construction considerations for dewatering, temporary excavation support and site preparation.
The scope of work comprised:
•  Nine (9) soil borings, B-01 through B-09, drilled to depths ranging 55 to 90 ft below existing ground
surface;
•  Installation of five (5) monitoring installations (three shallow standpipe piezometers screened in the
upper sand and two deep piezometers screened in the dense sand and gravel below El. 720.0);
•  Recovery of representative split-spoon (SPT) samples on 2.5 ft or 5 ft centers and thin-walled
(Shelby-tube) undisturbed samples of the CL clay at selected borings;
•  Laboratory classification, index and consolidation testing (ASTM D2435, ASTM D698, ASTM D1557);
•  Engineering analysis and preparation of this report.

3.2  Regional and Local Geology
Columbus, Ohio lies within the Till Plains section of the Central Lowland physiographic province. Regional
surficial geology is dominated by Wisconsinan-age glacial deposits — chiefly clay-rich till, glaciolacustrine silt
and clay, and outwash sand and gravel — overlying Devonian-age carbonate and shale bedrock. Local
hydrogeology is characterized by a shallow phreatic surface within the outwash and reworked outwash sands, a
laterally continuous fine-grained aquitard, and a lower confined aquifer within basal outwash sand and gravel
above bedrock.
The subsurface conditions encountered in the Package A borings are consistent with this regional framework: a
medium-dense reworked outwash sand at the surface, a low-permeability clay of glaciolacustrine origin at
intermediate depth, and a dense outwash sand and gravel aquifer at depth. Bedrock was not encountered within
the maximum boring depth of 90 ft (approximately El. 660.0). Blow counts in the SW-GW below El. 720.0
were consistently in the range N ≥ 50 blows per 6 inches, indicating a very dense sand-and-gravel deposit
suitable as a pile-bearing stratum.
3.3  Site History and Prior Use
Site historical review — including review of Franklin County parcel records, USGS topographic maps (1955
and later editions), and Thornbury State University campus master planning archives — indicates that the
Package A parcel was in agricultural use through approximately 1958, was acquired by the University in 1962,
and has been used for surface parking and landscape maintenance since. No prior structures of consequence, no
known below-grade utilities (other than a single abandoned 6-inch clay drain traced along the historic swale in
Block B), and no known industrial fill are present within the footprint. Because there is essentially no prior fill
of engineering significance, the Block B footprint requires new engineered fill — placed on the natural
clay-upper-sand contact after removal of the topsoil mantle — to bring the site to design grade.

7.2  Confined Piezometric Head — Deep Aquifer

rise in any well, boring or excavation that penetrates the clay and exposes the underlying aquifer. Any
excavation that either (a) penetrates the clay and enters the aquifer, or (b) reduces the effective weight of the
clay plug between the excavation subgrade and the top of the aquifer, will be subject to upward hydrostatic
pressure equal to the confined head above the point in question.

The 18-ft-thick CL clay aquitard is normally-consolidated (Section 5.2). Any net stress increase q applied at

the standard one-dimensional consolidation equation, in which Sc is the settlement and q the stress increase:
Sc  = Cc · H / (1 + e0) · log10[ (σ'0 + q) / σ'0 ]

•  Cc = 0.28

only marginally above σ'0, this threshold is exceeded by essentially any structural or fill load of engineering

8.3  Downdrag on Deep Foundations
The Block B footprint is raised approximately 12 ft above its natural surface by engineered fill placed
over a normally-consolidated CLAY 18 ft thick and of low permeability. Primary consolidation of that
clay under the weight of the new fill was in progress at the date of this issue and, on the coefficients
measured in the laboratory series, is expected to continue for a period measured in years rather than
months.
Deep foundations driven from the raised working grade pass through that consolidating layer. Where the
surrounding soil settles more than the pile, the relative movement at the pile-soil interface reverses:
the soil moves down past the shaft instead of the shaft moving down past the soil.
Over the depth in which that condition applies the interface shear acts downward on the pile. It is an
additional axial load carried by the pile, not a component of its resistance, and it is superimposed on
the structural load for as long as consolidation continues.
The magnitude depends on the thickness of the still-consolidating layer, the interface shear available
within it and the depth of the neutral plane. Requirements for its treatment in design are set out in
Section 9.3.

9.5  Engineered Fill Placement over the Clay
Bringing the Block B footprint to design grade requires placement of engineered fill of nominal 12 ft thickness
(from natural ground at El. 738.0 up to design grade at El. 750.0). Because there is no substantial engineered fill
or naturally overconsolidated material above the clay at Block B, the engineered fill is placed directly on the
stripped clay surface after topsoil removal only.
The engineered fill loads the underlying normally-consolidated CL clay as an areal surcharge, and consolidation
of the clay under the fill surcharge will occur. Under the parameters of Table 5-1, the settlement caused by 12 ft
of fill placed as a wide, essentially areal surcharge is substantial and will accrue over a period on the order of
years. The engineering consequences must be reconciled by the design team:

consolidation before piles are driven and the podium is erected, then the residual downdrag on the piles

•  The basement excavation for Blocks A and B, with a subgrade at approximately El. 731.5, is above the

SECTION 31 20 00
EARTH MOVING
Birchwood Village Expansion Program — Package A
Thornbury State University
Structural Engineer of Record: Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC
812 East Broad Street, Columbus, OH 43205
Revision: Rev.3  |  Issue Date: 03/06/2026  |  Supersedes: Rev.2 (issued 11/14/2025)
PART 1    GENERAL
1.1   SUMMARY
A.   Section Includes:
1.   Excavation, subgrade preparation, and grading for building foundations, mat foundations,
pile caps, footings, and slabs-on-grade within the Package A limits of work.
2.   Placement, moisture-conditioning, and compaction of engineered structural fill under
building foundations and slabs-on-grade.
3.   Backfill against foundation walls and around subsurface structures.
4.   Field quality control by the Owner's independent testing laboratory.
B.   Related Sections:
1.   Section 31 23 33 — Trenching and Backfilling for utility trenches within the building
envelope.
2.   Section 31 50 00 — Excavation Support and Protection for delegated shoring design.
3.   Section 03 30 00 — Cast-in-Place Concrete for placement of concrete against completed
subgrade.
1.2   REFERENCES
A.   Referenced Standards. The following standards are incorporated by reference to the extent
cited herein. The latest edition in effect at the date of Contract award shall govern.
1.   ASTM D698 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
Soil Using Standard Effort (Standard Proctor). Cited for historical borrow characterization
only; not the acceptance basis for Package A structural fill.
2.   ASTM D1557 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
Soil Using Modified Effort (Modified Proctor). Governing laboratory reference for
Package A structural fill.
3.   ASTM D6938 — Standard Test Methods for In-Place Density and Water Content of Soil
and Soil-Aggregate by Nuclear Methods (Shallow Depth). Governing field density test
method.
4.   ASTM D2216 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Determination of Water
(Moisture) Content of Soil and Rock by Mass. Referee method for moisture content
31 20 00 - Page 1 of 6
Earth Moving


========== PDF PAGE 2 ==========
when the nuclear gauge reading is disputed.
5.   ASTM D2937 — Standard Test Method for Density of Soil in Place by the Drive-Cylinder
Method. Alternate field density method where permitted in writing by the Structural
Engineer of Record.
1.3   DEFINITIONS
A.   Structural Fill: Imported or on-site engineered soil placed and compacted in controlled lifts
beneath building foundations, mat foundations, pile caps, footings, or slabs-on-grade, and
meeting the material, gradation, and compaction requirements of this Section.
B.   Common Fill: Non-structural earth used only for site grading outside the building envelope.
C.   Lift: A single layer of loose fill placed in preparation for compaction, not exceeding the
maximum loose lift thickness specified in Part 3.
D.   Test Location: A single field-density test point at which both dry density and moisture
content are measured for compliance evaluation.
E.   Placed Material: The specific soil material actually placed in the field at the test location,
whose laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content have been established
by ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory testing prior to placement, as required by Article 2.1.
1.4   QUALITY ASSURANCE
A.   Testing Laboratory. Field and laboratory testing under this Section shall be performed by the
Owner's independent construction materials testing laboratory (the “Laboratory”), contracted
directly to the Owner. The Contractor shall coordinate access, sampling opportunity, and
lift-by-lift notification with the Laboratory.
B.   Personnel. Nuclear-gauge operators shall hold current radiation safety training and shall be
documented as competent in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures. Nuclear gauges
shall be calibrated within the manufacturer's stated interval and standard-count checked at
the start of each testing day.
C.   Placed-Material Correspondence. The laboratory maximum dry density and optimum
moisture content used as the acceptance denominators for any test location shall be those
determined by ASTM D1557 Method C on the material actually placed at that location. Where
the placed material differs materially from the previously characterized borrow, a new ASTM
D1557 Method C test shall be performed on the new material before further fill placement is
accepted.
1.5   SUBMITTALS
A.   Prior to structural fill placement, submit for review:
1.   Source identification for each proposed borrow, including gradation (sieve analysis),
Atterberg limits, and USCS classification.
2.   Laboratory report of maximum dry density and optimum moisture content per ASTM
D1557 Method C for each proposed source material.
3.   Placement and compaction plan identifying lift thickness, compaction equipment, and
passes.
B.   During placement, submit daily:
31 20 00 - Page 2 of 6
Earth Moving


========== PDF PAGE 3 ==========
1.   Field density reports per ASTM D6938 identifying test location, lift number, elevation, dry
density, moisture content, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry density
and optimum moisture content used as denominators, percent compaction, and moisture
deviation from optimum.
1.6   SEQUENCING
A.   No structural fill shall be placed until the underlying subgrade has been proof-rolled in the
presence of the Laboratory and accepted in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer.
B.   No fill placement shall proceed on any lift until the preceding lift has been tested and
accepted per Article 3.4.
PART 2    PRODUCTS
2.1   STRUCTURAL FILL
A.   Material. Well-graded granular fill classified SM or SW-SM, laboratory-tested per ASTM
D1557 Method C (modified Proctor) prior to placement.
B.   Gradation. Structural fill shall meet the following gradation, with no more than 12% passing
the No. 200 sieve and a plasticity index not exceeding 6.
C.   Deleterious Material. Structural fill shall be free of organic material, frozen soil, debris, and
particles greater than 3 inches in largest dimension.
D.   Laboratory Characterization. For each source and for each material change, the Laboratory
shall determine the maximum dry density and optimum moisture content by ASTM D1557
Method C prior to placement. The resulting laboratory values are the denominators against
which the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B are evaluated.
2.2   COMMON FILL
A.   Common fill placed outside the building envelope shall be free of organic material, debris, and
frozen soil, but is not subject to the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B.
2.3   CAPILLARY BREAK / DRAINAGE COURSE
A.   Clean, open-graded crushed stone, 3/4 in nominal, less than 2% passing the No. 200 sieve,
placed as shown on the Drawings beneath slabs-on-grade.
PART 3    EXECUTION
3.1   EXAMINATION
A.   Examine subgrade prior to fill placement. Do not proceed with fill placement over subgrade
that is soft, yielding under proof roll, frozen, or otherwise unsuitable. Notify the Owner's
Representative Engineer in writing of any unsuitable subgrade condition.
3.2   SUBGRADE PREPARATION
A.   Strip topsoil, organic material, and any existing uncontrolled fill from beneath the footprint of
structural fill.
B.   Proof-roll exposed subgrade with a loaded tandem-axle dump truck or equivalent equipment
approved in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer. The Laboratory shall be present
31 20 00 - Page 3 of 6
Earth Moving


========== PDF PAGE 4 ==========
to witness the proof roll.
C.   Undercut and replace yielding areas with structural fill placed and compacted per this
Section.
3.3   PLACEMENT
A.   Place structural fill in horizontal lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose thickness.
B.   Moisture-condition each lift, by wetting or drying and mixing, so that the moisture content at
the time of compaction is within the range specified in Article 3.4.B.
C.   Compact each lift with equipment sized and operated to achieve the density and moisture
requirements of Article 3.4.B throughout the full thickness of the lift.
D.   Do not place fill on frozen subgrade or with frozen material. Do not place fill during
precipitation that raises the placed material's moisture content above the upper limit of Article
3.4.B.
3.4   COMPACTION
A.   Method Statement. The Contractor shall place structural fill in controlled lifts as specified in
Article 3.3, moisture-conditioning each lift as necessary to bring the material within the
moisture range required by Article 3.4.B before compaction. Compaction equipment
(self-propelled vibratory smooth-drum rollers, pad-foot rollers, or plate compactors adjacent to
structures) shall be operated in a pattern of overlapping passes such that every location
within a lift receives no fewer than the number of passes established during a
Contractor-conducted test strip witnessed by the Laboratory and the Owner's Representative
Engineer. The test strip shall be executed at the start of production placement, using the
placement source, moisture-conditioning method, lift thickness, and compaction equipment
intended for production, and shall demonstrate that the criteria of Article 3.4.B are met before
general production is authorized. Adjacent to walls, columns, and utilities, use hand-operated
compaction equipment in lifts not exceeding 6 inches loose thickness. Do not operate heavy
compaction equipment within 3 feet of walls prior to backfill balancing on both sides. Each lift
shall be tested and accepted per Article 3.4.B before the next lift is placed.
B.   Acceptance Criteria.
Structural fill shall be placed and compacted to a dry density of not less than
95% of the maximum dry density determined by ASTM D1557 Method C for the
placed material, AND shall be placed at a moisture content within −1% to +2%
of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test. Both criteria must
be satisfied for each test location. Field density shall be measured per ASTM
D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission mode) at a frequency of one test per
5,000 sf per lift.
C.   Failing Tests. Where either the density criterion or the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B is
not satisfied at any test location:
1.   The affected area of the lift shall be reworked (scarified, moisture-conditioned, and
recompacted, or removed and replaced) at the Contractor's expense.
2.   Reworked areas shall be retested by the Laboratory. Both the density and moisture
criteria of Article 3.4.B must be satisfied on the retest before the lift is accepted.
31 20 00 - Page 4 of 6
Earth Moving


========== PDF PAGE 5 ==========
3.   Isolated failing tests may not be averaged with adjacent passing tests to demonstrate
compliance. Acceptance is evaluated at each test location independently.
D.   Interpretation. No test location shall be accepted on the basis of density alone. No test
location shall be accepted on the basis of moisture alone. Compliance requires that both the
density criterion and the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B be independently satisfied at that
test location, as measured against the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry
density and optimum moisture content of the material actually placed at that location.
3.5   BACKFILL AGAINST FOUNDATION WALLS
A.   Do not commence backfill against basement or foundation walls until the wall has attained its
specified 28-day compressive strength, or until permanent lateral support (floor framing) is in
place and grouted to the wall, whichever occurs first.
B.   Place backfill on both sides of interior walls in balanced lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose
thickness, differing by no more than one lift side-to-side.
C.   Compact backfill to the same acceptance criteria as Article 3.4.B where the backfill supports
structure or slabs; elsewhere, to 90% of ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density.
3.6   SETTLEMENT TOLERANCE
A.   Total and Differential Settlement. Total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement
0.5 in maximum over 30 ft.
B.   Application. The tolerances of Paragraph A apply to the completed foundation system as
constructed on the accepted subgrade and structural fill delivered under this Section. Where
predicted or monitored settlements exceed the tolerances of Paragraph A, the Structural
Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a
written disposition is issued.
C.   Monitoring. Where settlement monitoring points are shown on the Drawings, readings shall
be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the frequency indicated.
Cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance of Paragraph A shall be reported
immediately.
3.7   FIELD QUALITY CONTROL
A.   Testing frequency for structural fill:
1.   In-place density and moisture: one ASTM D6938 test per 5,000 sf per lift, as required by
Article 3.4.B, and not fewer than three tests per lift regardless of lift area.
2.   Laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content: one ASTM D1557
Method C determination per source, and one additional determination for each material
change identified by visual classification or gradation.
B.   Reporting. The Laboratory shall issue field density reports within 24 hours of testing. Each
report shall identify, for each test location, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum
dry density and optimum moisture content used as the denominators, the measured dry
density, the measured moisture content, the percent compaction, the moisture deviation from
optimum, and the disposition (accept or reject) against Article 3.4.B.
C.   Non-Conforming Work. Any lift not meeting Article 3.4.B, or any lift for which the ASTM
D1557 Method C denominators used in reporting do not correspond to the material actually
placed, shall be reworked as required by Article 3.4.C before any additional lift is placed.

3.8   PROTECTION
A.   Protect accepted subgrade and completed structural fill from disturbance, softening by
precipitation, freezing, and construction traffic until covered by permanent construction.
Rework and retest, at the Contractor's expense, any area disturbed or softened prior to
permanent cover.

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
This memorandum establishes the governing codes, reference standards, site parameters, design loads, load
combinations, and serviceability criteria adopted for the structural design of Package A of the Birchwood Village
Expansion. Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared
podium, one basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
Block B. The design basis stated herein governs all Package A calculations, drawings, and specifications issued
by the Engineer of Record and controls the interpretation of subordinate design documents where a conflict
arises.
This Rev.2 issue supersedes Rev.1 dated 07/18/2025. Substantive changes since Rev.1 are recorded in the
Revision Block on the final page.
2. GOVERNING CODES AND REFERENCE STANDARDS
The Project is designed in accordance with the following:
• Ohio Building Code (2024 edition, adopting IBC 2021 with Ohio amendments) — governing building
code as adopted by the State of Ohio; Chapter 16 (Structural Design) references ASCE 7-16 for loads.
• ACI 318-19, Building Code Requirements for Structural Concrete and Commentary — reinforced concrete
design, detailing, cover, and serviceability.
• ASCE 7-16, Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and Other Structures — dead,
live, snow, wind, seismic loads and load combinations.
• AISC 360-16, Specification for Structural Steel Buildings — structural steel members and connections at
podium framing and roof.
• ACI 301-20 for cast-in-place concrete construction requirements referenced through Spec 03 30 00.
• ASCE 32-01 for frost-protected shallow foundations where applicable at Block C perimeter.
Materials and test methods are governed by the specifications listed in Section 03 20 00, 03 30 00, and 31 20 00
(Rev.2, current at the date of this memorandum), and where cited by ASTM designation on the drawings.
Where an inconsistency arises between the Ohio Building Code (adopting IBC 2021) and a referenced consensus
standard, the more stringent provision governs unless the Ohio amendment expressly modifies the standard.
3. SITE CONDITIONS SUMMARY
The following elevations and stratigraphy are adopted for structural design and are taken from the Kelbrook
Geotechnical Investigation Report — Package A (Rev.2, 02/14/2025) and from the Boring Logs and
Groundwater Monitoring Records (B-01 through B-09):

def sc_split(s0,ds):
    sf=s0+ds
    if sf<=sp: return Cr*HR*log(sf/s0)
    if s0>=sp: return Cc*HR*log(sf/s0)
    return Cr*HR*log(sp/s0)+Cc*HR*log(sf/sp)
for s0 in (1850.0, sv_mid-u_lin, sv_mid-u_hyd):
    print(f"s'0={s0:.0f}: ds=900 -> NC eqn {sc_nc(s0,900):.2f} in ; Cr-to-s'p-then-Cc {sc_split(s0,900):.2f} in ; recompression part {Cr*HR*log(sp/s0):.3f}")

for q in (100,300,600,1000,1200):
    print(f"  GIR T8-1 check q={q}: {sc_nc(1850,q):.2f}")
# allowable ds for Sc=1.0 and for Sc=0.1 (remaining after 0.90 immediate)
def solve(target,f):
    lo,hi=0.0,5000.0
    for _ in range(100):
        m=(lo+hi)/2
        if f(1850.0,m)>target: hi=m
        else: lo=m
    return m
print(f"ds giving Sc=1.00 in: NC {solve(1.0,sc_nc):.0f} psf ; split {solve(1.0,sc_split):.0f} psf")
print(f"ds giving Sc=0.10 in: NC {solve(0.10,sc_nc):.0f} psf ; split {solve(0.10,sc_split):.0f} psf")
# sublayer integration (3 x 6 ft) at uniform ds=900 for info
tot=0
for i in range(3):
    zc = TOPCLAY - 3 - 6*i
    sv = (GS-TOPCLAY)*g_sand + (TOPCLAY-zc)*g_clay
    s0 = 1850.0 + (zc-MID)*(-(g_clay-gw))  # scale about 1850 with buoyant gradient
    tot += Cc*(72/(1+e0))*log((s0+900)/s0)

# ---------- time rate ----------
cv_cm2s = 4.4e-4
cv = cv_cm2s*86400/929.0304
Hdr=9.0

for U,Tv in ((50,0.197),(90,0.848),(95,1.129)):

t=196
Tv=cv*t/Hdr**2
print(f"Tv at 196 d (instantaneous load at baseline) = {Tv:.3f}; U ~ {math.sqrt(4*Tv/math.pi)*100:.0f}%")

 5. SUMMARY
 Design water table adopted El. 742.0 ft; confined piezometric head El. 738.0 ft — both stable across monitoring
 period.

 The shallow SP-SM upper sand hosts an unconfined phreatic surface centered on El. 742.0, with all 57 individual
 shallow-piezometer readings (three piezometers × 19 rounds) falling within El. 741.6 to El. 742.4 across the 19-month
 monitoring period. The confined SW-GW sand and gravel aquifer below El. 720.0 exhibits a piezometric head centered on
 El. 738.0, with all 38 individual deep-piezometer readings (two piezometers × 19 rounds) falling within El. 737.7 to El.
 738.3 across the same period. The 18-ft-thick CL clay aquitard from El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0 separates the two
 regimes, and the two regimes have behaved independently across the monitoring record without evidence of hydraulic
 short-circuiting through the aquitard.

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Build the Item 051 verification memo on the Thelbridge template."""
import copy, datetime, re
import docx
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn

TPL = '/filesystem/Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_TEMPLATE_v1.docx'
OUT = '/filesystem/Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item051_BlockC.docx'
MEMO_DATE = '07/20/2026'

doc = docx.Document(TPL)
body = doc.element.body

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def make_run(text, size=10, bold=False, italic=False, color=None, va=None):
    r = OxmlElement('w:r')
    rPr = OxmlElement('w:rPr')
    f = OxmlElement('w:rFonts')
    for a in ('w:ascii', 'w:cs', 'w:eastAsia', 'w:hAnsi'):
        f.set(qn(a), 'Calibri')
    rPr.append(f)
    if bold:
        rPr.append(OxmlElement('w:b')); rPr.append(OxmlElement('w:bCs'))
    if italic:
        rPr.append(OxmlElement('w:i')); rPr.append(OxmlElement('w:iCs'))
    if color:
        c = OxmlElement('w:color'); c.set(qn('w:val'), color); rPr.append(c)
    for tag in ('w:sz', 'w:szCs'):
        s = OxmlElement(tag); s.set(qn('w:val'), str(int(round(size * 2)))); rPr.append(s)
    if va:
        v = OxmlElement('w:vertAlign'); v.set(qn('w:val'), va); rPr.append(v)
    r.append(rPr)
    parts = text.split('\t')
    for i, part in enumerate(parts):
        if i > 0:
            r.append(OxmlElement('w:tab'))
        if part:
            t = OxmlElement('w:t'); t.set(qn('xml:space'), 'preserve'); t.text = part
            r.append(t)
    return r

TOKEN = re.compile(r'(\*\*|//|_\{[^}]*\}|\^\{[^}]*\})')

def add_runs(p, text, size=10, bold=False, italic=False, color=None):
    """Mini markup: **bold**, //italic//, _{subscript}, ^{superscript}."""
    b, it = bold, italic
    for tok in TOKEN.split(text):
        if not tok:
            continue
        if tok == '**':
            b = not b; continue
        if tok == '//':
            it = not it; continue
        if tok.startswith('_{'):
            p.append(make_run(tok[2:-1], size, b, it, color, 'subscript')); continue
        if tok.startswith('^{'):
            p.append(make_run(tok[2:-1], size, b, it, color, 'superscript')); continue
        p.append(make_run(tok, size, b, it, color))

def make_par(text, size=10, bold=False, italic=False, color=None, after=80, before=0,
             left=0, hanging=0, keep_next=False, align=None, tabs=None, keep_lines=False):
    p = OxmlElement('w:p')
    pPr = OxmlElement('w:pPr')
    if keep_next:
        pPr.append(OxmlElement('w:keepNext'))
    if keep_lines:
        pPr.append(OxmlElement('w:keepLines'))
    if tabs:
        tb = OxmlElement('w:tabs')
        for pos in tabs:
            t = OxmlElement('w:tab'); t.set(qn('w:val'), 'left'); t.set(qn('w:pos'), str(pos))
            tb.append(t)
        pPr.append(tb)
    sp = OxmlElement('w:spacing'); sp.set(qn('w:before'), str(before)); sp.set(qn('w:after'), str(after))
    pPr.append(sp)
    if left or hanging:
        ind = OxmlElement('w:ind'); ind.set(qn('w:left'), str(left))
        if hanging:
            ind.set(qn('w:hanging'), str(hanging))
        pPr.append(ind)
    if align:
        jc = OxmlElement('w:jc'); jc.set(qn('w:val'), align); pPr.append(jc)
    p.append(pPr)
    add_runs(p, text, size, bold, italic, color)
    return p

def make_table(widths, rows, size=9, header=True, bold_first_col=False):
    tbl = OxmlElement('w:tbl')
    tblPr = OxmlElement('w:tblPr')
    w = OxmlElement('w:tblW'); w.set(qn('w:w'), str(sum(widths))); w.set(qn('w:type'), 'dxa'); tblPr.append(w)
    bd = OxmlElement('w:tblBorders')
    for side in ('top', 'left', 'bottom', 'right', 'insideH', 'insideV'):
        e = OxmlElement('w:' + side)
        e.set(qn('w:val'), 'single'); e.set(qn('w:sz'), '4'); e.set(qn('w:space'), '0'); e.set(qn('w:color'), 'A6A6A6')
        bd.append(e)
    tblPr.append(bd)
    lay = OxmlElement('w:tblLayout'); lay.set(qn('w:type'), 'fixed'); tblPr.append(lay)
    mar = OxmlElement('w:tblCellMar')
    for side, v in (('top', 30), ('left', 80), ('bottom', 30), ('right', 80)):
        m = OxmlElement('w:' + side); m.set(qn('w:w'), str(v)); m.set(qn('w:type'), 'dxa'); mar.append(m)
    tblPr.append(mar)
    look = OxmlElement('w:tblLook'); look.set(qn('w:val'), '04A0'); tblPr.append(look)
    tbl.append(tblPr)
    grid = OxmlElement('w:tblGrid')
    for wd in widths:
        g = OxmlElement('w:gridCol'); g.set(qn('w:w'), str(wd)); grid.append(g)
    tbl.append(grid)
    for ri, row in enumerate(rows):
        tr = OxmlElement('w:tr')
        trPr = OxmlElement('w:trPr')
        if ri == 0 and header:
            trPr.append(OxmlElement('w:tblHeader'))
        tr.append(trPr)
        for ci, cell in enumerate(row):
            tc = OxmlElement('w:tc')
            tcPr = OxmlElement('w:tcPr')
            tw = OxmlElement('w:tcW'); tw.set(qn('w:w'), str(widths[ci])); tw.set(qn('w:type'), 'dxa'); tcPr.append(tw)
            if ri == 0 and header:
                shd = OxmlElement('w:shd'); shd.set(qn('w:val'), 'clear'); shd.set(qn('w:color'), 'auto'); shd.set(qn('w:fill'), 'EDEDED')
                tcPr.append(shd)
            tc.append(tcPr)
            hb = (ri == 0 and header) or (bold_first_col and ci == 0)
            for line in cell.split('\n'):
                tc.append(make_par(line, size=size, bold=hb, after=20))
            tr.append(tc)
        tbl.append(tr)
    return tbl

def find_par(pred):
    for p in doc.paragraphs:
        if pred(p.text):
            return p
    raise KeyError

def insert_before(anchor, elements):
    for e in elements:
        anchor.addprevious(e)

# convenience constructors (twips)
def P(t, **k):            return make_par(t, **k)
def SUB(t):               return make_par(t, bold=True, before=120, after=60, keep_next=True)
def FH(t):                return make_par(t, bold=True, before=160, after=60, keep_next=True, keep_lines=True)
def ITEM(lbl, t, **k):    return make_par(lbl + '\t' + t, left=400, hanging=400, tabs=[400], **k)
def EQ(t):                return make_par(t, left=720, after=60)
def NOTE(t):              return make_par(t, size=8.5, color='404040', after=100)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- header block
def set_header_line(par, label, value):
    pPr = par._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    # remove existing tabs / ind, then insert in schema order (after pBdr, before spacing)
    for tag in ('w:tabs', 'w:ind'):
        for e in pPr.findall(qn(tag)):
            pPr.remove(e)
    tabs = OxmlElement('w:tabs'); t = OxmlElement('w:tab'); t.set(qn('w:val'), 'left'); t.set(qn('w:pos'), '1200'); tabs.append(t)
    ind = OxmlElement('w:ind'); ind.set(qn('w:left'), '1200'); ind.set(qn('w:hanging'), '1200')
    sp = pPr.find(qn('w:spacing'))
    if sp is not None:
        sp.addprevious(tabs); sp.addnext(ind)
    else:
        pPr.append(tabs); pPr.append(ind)
    for r in list(par._p.findall(qn('w:r'))):
        par._p.remove(r)
    par._p.append(make_run(label, 10, bold=True))
    par._p.append(make_run('\t' + value, 10))

p_to = find_par(lambda s: s.startswith('To:'))
p_from = find_par(lambda s: s == 'From:')
p_date = find_par(lambda s: s == 'Date:')
p_subj = find_par(lambda s: s == 'Subject:')

set_header_line(p_to, 'To:', "Adrian Vance, Project Engineer (Structural/Geotechnical), Owner's Representative")
set_header_line(p_from, 'From:', 'Rahul Nimkar, Geotechnical Reviewer')
cc_el = copy.deepcopy(p_from._p)
p_from._p.addnext(cc_el)
p_cc = docx.text.paragraph.Paragraph(cc_el, p_from._parent)
set_header_line(p_cc, 'cc:', 'Rachel Marlbeck, University Program Director, Thornbury State University, Office of Capital Programs')
set_header_line(p_date, 'Date:', MEMO_DATE)
set_header_line(p_subj, 'Subject:', 'Verification Register Item 051 — Block C Spread Footings: Long-Term Settlement of the '
                'Stratum 2 Clay (Calculation CB-GEO-007 Rev.0) — NOT VERIFIED')

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- section content
def section_anchor(heading_start):
    h = find_par(lambda s: s.startswith(heading_start))
    guide = h._p.getnext()            # italic guidance paragraph
    empty = guide.getnext()           # empty placeholder paragraph
    return h, guide, empty

S = {}

# ---- 1. PURPOSE
S['1.'] = [
    P("This memorandum records the geotechnical verification of Item 051 on the Thelbridge Review Comment and "
      "Verification Register — Package A (D14, REGISTER sheet, row 53; raised 07/10/2026; required by 07/20/2026). "
      "Item 051 requires Thelbridge to verify the Block C spread-footing foundations for long-term settlement over the "
      "compressible Stratum 2 CL clay (C_{c} 0.28, e_{0} 0.92, σ'_{p} 1,900 psf, 18 ft thick) under a stress increase Δσ of "

      after=60),
]

# ---- 2. DOCUMENTS REVIEWED

S['2.'] = [
    P("The documents relied on are listed below. The references D1 to D19 are used in Sections 3 to 5. Page numbers are "
      "the printed page numbers of each document; workbook references give the sheet and row.", after=100),
    make_table([620, 5600, 2200, 1300], docs_rows, size=9),

# ---- 3. BASIS OF REVIEW
S['3.'] = [
    SUB('3.1  Governing requirements'),
    ITEM('(a)', "**Specification 31 20 00 Rev.3, Article 3.6 (D7, p. 5 of 6).** 3.6.A: total settlement 1.0 in maximum; "

    # ---------------- Finding 1
    FH("Finding 1 — The long-term consolidation settlement of the clay has not been computed. CB-GEO-007 is incomplete."),
    P("CB-GEO-007 Sheet 4 (“Consolidation”, D1) shows σ'_{0}, Δσ, σ'_{p}, H, C_{c}, e_{0} and the result as “—” and states: "

VERIFICATION MEMORANDUM

From:Rahul Nimkar, Geotechnical Reviewer

Subject:Verification Register Item 051 — Block C Spread Footings: Long-Term Settlement of the Stratum 2 Clay (Calculation CB-GEO-007 Rev.0) — NOT VERIFIED
1.  PURPOSE
This memorandum records the geotechnical verification of Item 051 on the Thelbridge Review Comment and Verification Register — Package A (D14, REGISTER sheet, row 53; raised 07/10/2026; required by 07/20/2026). Item 051 requires Thelbridge to verify the Block C spread-footing foundations for long-term settlement over the compressible Stratum 2 CL clay (Cc 0.28, e0 0.92, σ'p 1,900 psf, 18 ft thick) under a stress increase Δσ of 900 psf at mid-layer, against a tolerance of 1 in total and 0.5 in differential; to confirm that the settlement analysis is complete and reconciled with the project tolerances; and to correlate it with the monitoring reading of 0.61 in cumulative on 06/26/2026.
The question to be determined is whether the Engineer of Record's (EOR's) analysis, Calculation CB-GEO-007 Rev.0 (Calloway Braddock, 09/30/2025), demonstrates that settlement of the Block C footings will stay within Specification 31 20 00 Rev.3, Article 3.6.A, so that the item can be closed. For this item, the memorandum also gives the status the Owner asked for by 07/20/2026 in R. Marlbeck's directive of 07/06/2026 (D16). It covers Item 051 only. Items 048 and 049 and the groundwater component of Item 056 are reported separately.
Outcome: NOT VERIFIED. The basis is set out in Section 4, and the disposition and required actions in Section 5.
2.  DOCUMENTS REVIEWED
The documents relied on are listed below. The references D1 to D16 are used in Sections 3 to 5. Page numbers are the printed page numbers of each document; workbook references give the sheet and row.

D12 | Submittal 03-SD-L3, Reinforcing Steel Shop Drawings, Level-3 Slab Cage (EOR review 06/18/2026) | Rev.1 | 06/12/2026
D13 | Field Observation Report, Excavation and Groundwater — Kelbrook Geotechnical | KGI-FO-2026-0528 | 05/28/2026
D14 | Thelbridge Review Comment and Verification Register — Package A (COVER, REGISTER, REVIEWER ASSIGNMENTS, REFERENCE VALUES, SCHEDULE) | Register — Package A | 07/15/2026
D15 | Submittal Register — Package A (entry 31-BM-B, Settlement Monitoring Program — Block C) | Register — Package A | 07/13/2026
D16 | Owner directive, R. Marlbeck to A. Vance, “Written Verification Required Before Permanent Work” (e-mail) | — | 07/06/2026

3.  BASIS OF REVIEW
3.1  Governing requirements
(a)Specification 31 20 00 Rev.3, Article 3.6 (D7, p. 5 of 6). 3.6.A: total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement 0.5 in maximum over 30 ft. 3.6.B: the tolerances apply to the completed foundation system. Where predicted or monitored settlements exceed them, the Structural Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing, and no additional load shall be applied until a written disposition is issued. 3.6.C: readings go to the Owner's Representative Engineer, and cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance shall be reported immediately.
(b)Design Basis Memorandum CB-DBM-001 Rev.2 (D6). §7.3 (p. 8): Block C settlement is checked in CB-GEO-007 under service-level combinations against Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6. §9 (p. 9): the geotechnical report controls all soil parameters, and any conflict is resolved in its favour.
(c)Geotechnical Investigation Report KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2 (D2). Table 5-1 (p. 11) sets the clay parameters. §8.1 (pp. 14–15) gives the consolidation equation and requires the Block C stress increase at mid-depth of the clay to be computed for each footing (or the governing footing). §9.1 (pp. 16–17) requires the EOR to “explicitly compute consolidation settlement of the clay … using the parameters in Table 5-1” and to reconcile it with the total and differential tolerances. If they are exceeded, it lists larger footings, a mat or deep foundations.
(d)Laboratory report VMT-2025-0109-CON (D4), Summary — Design Params sheet, Design Statement of Applicability (row 38): because σ'p exceeds σ'0 by only about 50 psf, any net stress increase is governed by Cc, not Cr.
(e)Register Item 051 scope and conventions (D14): REGISTER row 53; COVER row 28 (disposition terms VERIFIED / VERIFIED WITH COMMENT / NOT VERIFIED).
3.2  Review method
(1)Completeness: whether CB-GEO-007 contains each element that GIR §9.1 and DBM §7.3 require.
(2)Inputs and traceability: each CB-GEO-007 parameter checked against D2 to D5; the foundation geometry checked against D6, D8, D9 and D11; references traced to their source.
(3)Independent check of primary consolidation for a single layer at mid-depth (El. 729.0), as GIR §8.1 and the register item frame it. Inputs: H/(1 + e0) = 216 in / 1.92 = 112.5 in; γw = 62.4 pcf. Two forms were used:
GIR §8.1 form:   Sc = Cc · H/(1 + e0) · log10[(σ'0 + Δσ) / σ'0]
Stress-history form:   Sc = Cr · H/(1 + e0) · log10(σ'p / σ'0) + Cc · H/(1 + e0) · log10[(σ'0 + Δσ) / σ'p]
Sensitivity was run on σ'0 and Δσ. The stress increase was checked by Boussinesq (Newmark integration over uniformly loaded rectangles, superposing the twelve footings of the CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 schedule) and by the 2:1 method. Time rate was taken from Terzaghi one-dimensional theory, using the laboratory cv and a 9 ft drainage path (drainage to both faces of the clay, D2 p. 15).
(4)Correlation of the monitoring record (D11) with CB-GEO-007 and with consolidation theory: magnitude, rate, differential and groundwater.
The independent check is a verification tool. It does not replace the EOR's analysis or transfer design responsibility to Thelbridge.
4.  FINDINGS
Finding 1 — The long-term consolidation settlement of the clay has not been computed. CB-GEO-007 is incomplete.
CB-GEO-007 Sheet 4 (“Consolidation”, D1) shows σ'0, Δσ, σ'p, H, Cc, e0 and the result as “—” and states: “Not computed. Serviceability taken from the immediate settlement result on Sheet 3.” Sheet 5 tabulates the clay parameters “for the record” and states that the governing serviceability check is on Sheet 3 (row 21). The conclusion “Block C spread footing serviceability — SATISFACTORY” (Sheet 3, row 70) rests only on Schmertmann immediate settlement: maximum 0.90 in at F-C6 and maximum differential 0.20 in. Sheet 3 is itself a short-term calculation (creep factor C2 = 1.00 at t = 0.1 yr, row 8).
The omitted component is the one the geotechnical record identifies as governing: GIR §9.1 (pp. 16–17), §8.1 (pp. 14–15) and Executive Summary Recommendation 1 (p. 6), and the Vantree Design Statement (D4). Schmertmann's strain-influence method is an elastic method developed for granular soils. The clay sublayers on Sheet 3 use an undrained modulus back-figured from CU triaxial tests (row 15), which represents constant-volume distortion only. It cannot capture the volume change of the clay as excess pore pressure dissipates. I checked the Sheet 3 arithmetic for F-C6 (C1 = 0.86, ΣIz·Δz/Es = 0.0468 ft/tsf, Si = 0.90 in) and it reproduces. The immediate component is not examined further here because it does not govern.
The settlement analysis is therefore not complete, and the Sheet 3 “SATISFACTORY” conclusion does not address the long-term condition that Item 051 covers.
Finding 2 — The clay parameters are correctly transcribed. The stress path lies on the virgin branch, and the σ'0 derivation needs to be stated.
The Stratum 2 values on CB-GEO-007 Sheets 2 and 5 agree with the sources: Cc 0.28, Cr 0.045, e0 0.92, σ'p 1,900 psf, σ'0 1,850 psf (OCR 1.03), cv 4.5 × 10−4 cm²/s, H 18 ft (El. 738.0 to El. 720.0) with double drainage; unit weights 118/120/130 pcf; design water table El. 742.0 (D4, B-06 U3 sheet rows 92–98 and Summary sheet rows 8–19; D2, Table 5-1 p. 11 and Table 6-1 p. 12; D5, SUMMARY sheet). Boring B-09 at the centre of Block C (D3, p. 12) confirms the profile there: SP-SM to El. 738.0, CL clay from El. 738.0 to El. 720.0, water at El. 741.8 (24-hour reading El. 742.0). The sample elevations on Sheet 5 (El. 727.5 and El. 731.0) differ from D4/D5 (El. 729.5 and El. 728.7), which does not affect the parameters.
(a)Virgin branch governs. σ'0 + Δσ = 1,850 + 900 = 2,750 psf, which exceeds σ'p = 1,900 psf by 850 psf. Cr applies only to the first 50 psf. Applying Cr to the whole increment would give 5.06 × log10(2,750/1,850) ≈ 0.9 in and would understate the settlement by a factor of about six.
(b)σ'0 derivation. The value of 1,850 psf (D2 Table 5-1; D4 B-06 U3 row 93, “from soil profile / γt and water table El. 742.0”) could not be reproduced exactly. Total stress at El. 729.0 is 12 × 118 + 9 × 120 = 2,496 psf. Hydrostatic pore pressure from El. 742.0 (13 × 62.4 = 811 psf) gives σ'0 ≈ 1,685 psf. Allowing for the downward gradient to the confined head at El. 738.0 (pore pressure 250 psf at the top of the clay and 1,123 psf at its base, so 686 psf at mid-depth) gives ≈ 1,810 psf. Finding 3 shows that the outcome does not depend on which value is used. The revised calculation must nonetheless state the derivation it adopts.
Finding 3 — Independent check: consolidation settlement under the register inputs is about 5 in, five times the 1.0 in total tolerance.
With Δσ = 900 psf at El. 729.0 and the Table 5-1 parameters:
GIR §8.1 form:   Sc = 0.28 × 112.5 × log10(2,750/1,850) = 31.50 × 0.1722 = 5.4 in
Stress-history form:   Sc = 0.045 × 112.5 × log10(1,900/1,850) + 0.28 × 112.5 × log10(2,750/1,900) = 0.06 + 5.06 = 5.1 in
As a control on my use of the §8.1 equation, I reproduced GIR Table 8-1 (p. 15): 0.72, 2.06, 3.84, 5.91 and 6.84 in for q = 100, 300, 600, 1,000 and 1,200 psf, against 0.7, 2.1, 3.8, 5.9 and 6.8 in tabulated. Consolidation alone is therefore 5.1 to 5.4 in, before any immediate settlement is added. Adding the 0.90 in from Sheet 3 gives about 6.0 to 6.3 in, against a 1.0 in limit.
Case | σ'0 (psf) | Δσ at mid-clay (psf) | Sc (in) 1
1  Register / CB-GEO-007 inputs | 1,850 | 900 | 5.1 – 5.4
2  σ'0 from hydrostatic pore pressure (El. 742.0) | 1,685 | 900 | 4.5 – 5.9
3  σ'0 allowing for downward gradient to the El. 738.0 head | 1,810 | 900 | 5.0 – 5.5
4  Beneath footing centres, CB-GEO-007 schedule (Finding 4) 2 | 1,850 | 780 – 1,190 | 4.5 – 6.8
5  S-201 Detail 3 footing (7'-6" square, underside El. 746.0, 4,000 psf), single footing 2 | 1,850 | 340 – 375 | 2.0 – 2.5
1 Lower value: stress-history form; upper value: GIR §8.1 form.   2 Indicative; depends on the footing geometry, which is unresolved (Finding 5).
Every case is at least twice the tolerance, so the conclusion does not depend on how Findings 2, 4 and 5 are resolved. To keep Sc at or below 1.0 in, the mid-clay stress increase would have to be no more than about 140 psf (GIR form) to 185 psf (stress-history form). Once the 0.90 in immediate settlement is counted, only about 0.1 in remains for consolidation, which corresponds to 15 to 55 psf. The single mid-depth calculation is also not an upper bound where a footing bears only 2.5 ft above the clay: an indicative six-sublayer calculation beneath F-C6 gives about 7.9 in.
Time rate: with cv = 4.4 × 10−4 cm²/s (about 0.041 ft²/day; D4 Summary rows 17 and 30) and a 9 ft drainage path, t50 ≈ 1.1 years and t90 ≈ 4.6 years (Tv = 0.197 and 0.848). This is consistent with GIR p. 15 (“several years”). Most of the settlement would therefore develop after finishes are installed and the building is occupied.
Finding 4 — The 900 psf stress increase cannot be reproduced at the location stated and is not the governing value. Differential settlement is not demonstrated, and the criterion applied is not the governing one.
CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 (rows 39–41) describes Δσ ≈ 900 psf as the “combined stress bulb from adjacent footings (interior mid-block point, El. 729.0)”, obtained by “Boussinesq superposition, four adjacent footings at grid centre, 2:1 method verification”. I modelled the Sheet 2 schedule: footing sizes and qnet, a 26 ft × 24 ft grid on the layout implied by the Sheet 2 designations (the same layout as the D11 grid), and underside El. 740.5, i.e., 11.5 ft above El. 729.0. The results:
(a)Bay centres: about 260 to 310 psf by Boussinesq superposition of all twelve footings, and zero by the 2:1 method. The 2:1 spread of a 10.5 ft footing at 11.5 ft depth extends 11 ft from its centre, short of the 12 to 13 ft offset to the bay centre.
(b)Beneath footing centres: about 780 psf (F-C12) to 1,190 psf (F-C6) by Boussinesq; 850 psf for F-C6 alone by the 2:1 method.
The 900 psf therefore does not correspond to the location stated, and it is not the governing value beneath a footing centreline. A single value also cannot support a differential settlement check: GIR §8.1 (pp. 14–15) requires the stress increase for each footing.
Differential settlement. The Sheet 3 check (rows 55–67) uses immediate settlement only, and its geometry does not match the Sheet 2 schedule. F-C6–F-C12 is recorded as 35.8 ft apart, but C12 is two bays from C6 (about 57 ft). F-C11, an edge footing diagonally adjacent to C6 (about 35 ft), is recorded as the “opposite corner” at 62.4 ft. Consolidation depends on footing size and position, so it will not be uniform. With the footing-centre stresses above, the indicative difference in consolidation settlement between adjacent 10.5 ft and 8.5 ft footings 24 ft apart is about 1.4 to 1.6 in (F-C1/F-C5 about 1.6 in, roughly 1/180), and 11 of the 17 adjacent pairs exceed 0.5 in.
Criterion. CB-GEO-007 (Cover, rows 23–26) adopts 0.5 in between adjacent footings plus an angular distortion of 1/500, citing AISC Design Guide 3, Bjerrum and an “Owner's Basis of Design memo (Rev.1, 06/12/2025)”, which is not in the project record reviewed. The governing criterion is Spec 31 20 00 Art. 3.6.A, 0.5 in over 30 ft (D7, p. 5), as DBM §7.3 directs (D6, p. 8). That equals an angular distortion of about 1/720 and is more restrictive than 1/500.
Finding 5 — The foundation analysed does not match the issued drawings, the as-built basis is not established, and several references cannot be traced.
(a)CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2: twelve isolated square footings, 8.5 to 10.5 ft, underside El. 740.5. That is 2.5 ft above the clay and 1.5 ft below the design water table. The grid is 24 ft × 26 ft and the layout is taken “per S-101 Foundation Plan Rev.2 (09/12/2025)”. Footings are sized for 4,000 psf “per Kelbrook GIR Rev.2, §5.4” (rows 6, 16, 20–31, 36 and 37).
(b)S-201 Rev.4, Detail 3 (D9) shows a typical interior footing 7'-6" × 7'-6" × 2'-0", top El. 748.0, underside El. 746.0, with an allowable bearing pressure of 4,000 psf net. DBM §9 (D6, p. 9) gives 4,000 psf net “at El. 748 ± 2 ft”.
(c)S-101 Rev.4 (D8) places Block C on column grid B–L / 6–8, with 30 footing symbols, “isolated and combined spread footings” and a bottom-of-footing elevation that “varies — see S-201/3”. S-201 Detail 3 refers back to S-101 for the footing schedule, and neither sheet contains one. The S-101 revision block records Rev.2 as 12/12/2025, after the calculation date, and shows no issue dated 09/12/2025.
(d)The monitoring record (D11, Monitoring Points sheet) lists footings from 8.5 × 8.5 × 30 in to 10.5 × 10.5 × 36 in, matching the CB-GEO-007 sizes. It places them at “grid A/1” to “D/3”, a grid that does not appear on S-101 Rev.4. A bearing level of El. 740.5 would be below the water table, yet the record shows no dewatering for Block C: dewatering was limited to the Block A footprint (D14, Item 005), and P-09 stayed at El. 741.6 to 742.4 (D13 §5.3, p. 5).
(e)The GIR has no §5.4 and gives no allowable bearing pressure. §5.2, which Sheet 3 cites for the sand modulus, covers consolidation testing. §4.3, which Sheet 5 cites for thickness and drainage, covers instrumentation. The column loads are attributed to “CB-24-118 structural model Rev.A (issued 09/22/2025)”, and CB-GEO-007 carries firm project number CB-24-118 (Cover, rows 13 and 20). The other EOR documents in the record that carry a project number (S-101, S-102, S-201, CB-STR-011) use CB-2024-0417. The load source therefore cannot be traced to the Package A record.
The bearing level drives the analysis. The distance from footing base to mid-clay is 11.5 ft at El. 740.5 and 17.0 ft at El. 746.0, and Δσ and settlement change with it (Finding 3, cases 4 and 5). Combined footings, and any footings under the shear-wall bearing system described in DBM §7.5–7.6 (D6, p. 8), are not analysed. Bearing capacity is outside the scope of Item 051, but footing size controls Δσ. The revised analysis must use the as-built footing schedule, and the drawings must be made consistent with it.
Finding 6 — The monitoring record does not support the CB-GEO-007 conclusion.
The record (D11) comprises 12 points (MP-1 to MP-12) on the pedestal tops. The baseline was taken on 12/12/2025, after the footings were complete and backfilled, and 15 rounds of closed-loop precise levelling followed to 06/26/2026 (±0.01 in differential precision).
(a)Magnitude. The maximum is 0.61 in at MP-7 (FTG-C7); the other points read 0.31 to 0.58 in (Readings sheet, row 19). Load then in place over Block C comprised the Level-1 columns, Level-2 slab framing and CMU partitions, Level-3 framing, roof steel and the podium slab-on-grade (Notes sheet, rows 8–11). Finishes, the balance of superimposed dead load and occupancy live load had not yet been applied. MP-7 has nonetheless reached 74% of the full-load settlement predicted for F-C7 on Sheet 3 (0.82 in) and 61% of the 1.0 in tolerance.
(b)Rate. At MP-7 the 14-day increment rose from 0.03 in in each of the first three intervals to 0.06, 0.06 and 0.07 in in the last three (rows 24–37), i.e., from about 0.002 to 0.005 in/day. The survey party records the rate as “not decreasing” and “not yet stabilized” (Cover rows 35–36; Notes row 14; Trend Chart row 33). At the latest rate, with no further load and no further acceleration, MP-7 would reach 1.0 in in about 78 days, around 09/12/2026.
(c)Differential. The largest difference between adjacent points is already 0.23 in (MP-3/MP-7 and MP-8/MP-12, 24 ft apart on the CB-GEO-007 grid). That is more than the 0.20 in maximum differential CB-GEO-007 predicts at full load. The distribution also departs from the predicted pattern: corner point MP-4 (0.55 in, 77% of its predicted value) has settled more than edge point MP-3 (0.38 in, 48%).
(d)Groundwater. P-09 at Block C read El. 741.6 to 742.4 throughout (D3, Table 4-1, p. 13). The settlement is not caused by a lowered water table.
(e)Theory. Even if the whole load had been applied on the baseline date, the time factor at 196 days would be Tv ≈ 0.10, an average degree of consolidation of about 36%. Load was in fact added progressively, so the readings capture only the early part of the consolidation settlement.
The record shows settlement already near the CB-GEO-007 full-load prediction, a growing differential and no deceleration. It is consistent with the GIR's expectation that consolidation governs. Art. 3.6.C requires cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance to be reported immediately. No round after 06/26/2026 is in the record, although the 14-day cadence implies one on or about 07/10/2026.
Finding 7 — Article 3.6.B is engaged, and the extent of further loading on Block C needs to be confirmed.
Art. 3.6.B (D7, p. 5) applies where “predicted or monitored settlements exceed the tolerances”. The settlement predicted on the record (Findings 3 and 4) exceeds Art. 3.6.A. The EOR is therefore to be notified in writing, and no additional load is to be applied until the EOR issues a written disposition.
(a)Level-3 placement on 07/22/2026. The register SCHEDULE (D14) ties the hold-point to Items 052, 053 and 057, supported by 050 and 055. Item 051 is not listed, and the register COVER describes the placement as Block A/B. However, Submittal 03-SD-L3 Rev.1 (D12, Sheets 2 and 3 of 11, marks BM-02, BM-04, BM-16 and BM-18) details the Level-3 slab mats east–west over Grids 1–8, and S-101 Rev.4 places Block C on Grids 6–8. The extent of the 07/22/2026 placement over Block C is therefore not confirmed. Any part that bears on the Block C foundations would be additional load under Art. 3.6.B.
(b)Podium interface. S-310 Rev.4 (D10, Note 1) shows the podium continuous over Blocks A, B and C, and DBM §7.6 (D6, p. 8) couples the blocks through the podium diaphragm. Settlement of the Block C footings on the scale indicated would be imposed on the podium where it meets the pile-supported Block B and mat-supported Block A foundations. The EOR's disposition must address that interface as well as the Block C footings.
5.  CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION
5.1  Determination
The long-term settlement of the Block C spread footings is not verified. CB-GEO-007 Rev.0 omits the consolidation settlement of the Stratum 2 clay, which GIR §9.1 requires to be computed explicitly. It is not reconciled with Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Art. 3.6.A, and it rests on a stress increase and a footing geometry that cannot be reproduced or traced to the issued drawings (Findings 1, 4 and 5). On the register's own inputs, the independent check gives about 5 in of consolidation settlement (about 6 in total) against a 1.0 in tolerance, with differential settlement likely to exceed 0.5 in (Findings 3 and 4). The monitoring record does not support the CB-GEO-007 conclusion (Finding 6). The exceedance is large. Recalculation alone is unlikely to resolve it. The EOR's disposition is likely to require foundation measures at Block C, and the Owner should allow for the cost and programme effects.
5.2  Disposition
Item 051: NOT VERIFIED. Register status: Open (verification date “—”). The item cannot be closed by 07/20/2026 and should be reported to the Owner as not cleared in the status requested in D16.
5.3  Immediate actions
(1)A. Vance to transmit this memorandum to the EOR as the written notification required by Art. 3.6.B.
(2)No additional load to be applied to the Block C foundations until the EOR's written disposition (R1) has been issued and reviewed by Thelbridge. This includes any part of the 07/22/2026 Level-3 placement that bears on Block C.
(3)A. Vance to confirm with Rowan Bay, before release, whether any part of the 07/22/2026 placement bears on Block C (Grids 6–8). Release of the Block A/B scope is governed by Items 052, 053 and 057, supported by 050 and 055. Item 051 does not hold that scope, provided no part of the placement bears on Block C. Hold-point release remains with A. Vance.
5.4  Required before Item 051 can be closed

steps.message:
The Item 051 memo is written on your template, from Rahul Nimkar to Adrian Vance, cc Rachel Marlbeck, dated 07/20/2026. The disposition is **NOT VERIFIED** and the item stays **Open**; it can't be closed by 07/20.

**Why it fails**
- **The long-term calculation was never done.** In the Engineer of Record's settlement calculation (CB-GEO-007), the consolidation sheet says "Not computed". The "satisfactory" conclusion rests only on short-term settlement (0.90 in). The geotechnical report requires the clay consolidation to be computed explicitly.
- **My check gives about 5 in.** Using the register's own inputs, consolidation of the clay comes to about 5.1–5.4 in, or about 6 in with the short-term settlement added. The tolerance is 1.0 in. Every alternative I tried still gives at least 2 in, so the answer doesn't depend on the open questions below.
- **The 900 psf stress increase can't be reproduced.** At the point the calculation names it comes out at about 260–310 psf; under the footings it is about 780–1,190 psf. On an indicative check, 11 of 17 adjacent footing pairs exceed the 0.5 in differential limit. The calculation also uses a looser differential criterion than the spec's "0.5 in over 30 ft".
- **The calculation doesn't match the drawings.** It uses footings up to 10.5 ft square bearing at El. 740.5. Drawing S-201 Rev.4 shows a 7'-6" footing bearing at El. 746.0. Neither S-101 nor S-201 carries a footing schedule, and the calculation's load source and project number can't be traced. Nothing in the record establishes what was actually built.
- **Monitoring doesn't support the calculation.** The 0.61 in at the worst point is already 74% of its predicted full-load value, with the building only partly loaded. The rate has more than doubled. At the current rate that point reaches 1.0 in around 09/12/2026. The worst adjacent difference (0.23 in) already exceeds the calculation's full-load prediction.

**Effect on the 07/22 placement:** predicted settlement over tolerance triggers Spec 31 20 00 Art. 3.6.B. The EOR must be told in writing, and no further load goes on Block C until he issues a written disposition. The register describes the Level-3 placement as Block A/B, but the shop-drawing bar list runs across Grids 1–8, which includes Block C. Adrian should confirm the extent before release. Item 051 doesn't hold the Block A/B portion.

**What has to be produced, and by whom** (table R1–R7 in the memo)
- **Gregory Nash (EOR):**
  - the Art. 3.6.B written disposition;
  - a revised, sealed CB-GEO-007 that includes consolidation;
  - a reconciled footing schedule;
  - a remedial plan if the exceedance is confirmed, which is likely.
- **Rowan Bay:**
  - readings taken since 06/26 (the round due about 07/10 isn't in the record);
  - weekly readings until the EOR disposes;
  - a revised monitoring program;
  - the as-built footing record;
  - no further load on Block C.
- **Kelbrook,** through the Owner: review and concurrence on the revised analysis.

**Before it goes out**
- The signature line is blank for Rahul to sign.
- I added a cc line, since the template has none; the five sections are unchanged.
- The by-dates I put in (08/03 for the revised calculation, 07/27 for the contractor's records) are my recommendations. Adjust them if Adrian has agreed something else.
